title: Erdős Problem #852: Maximal Runs of Distinct Consecutive Prime Gaps
description: Let h(x) be the maximal length of a sequence of consecutive distinct prime gaps among primes below x. Is h(x) > (log x)^c? Is h(x) = o(log x)? Brun's sieve shows h(x) → ∞.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős posed this question about the structure of consecutive prime gaps in 1985. The problem asks for the growth rate of h(x), the maximal length of a run of distinct consecutive prime gaps below x. Brun's sieve establishes that h(x) → ∞, but the precise growth rate remains unknown.
overview.problemStatement: Let dₙ = pₙ₊₁ − pₙ. Define h(x) as the maximal k such that some consecutive run dₙ, dₙ₊₁, …, dₙ₊ₖ₋₁ with pₙ < x has all distinct values. Is h(x) > (log x)^c for some c > 0? Is h(x) = o(log x)?
overview.proofStrategy: We axiomatize the prime sequence and prime gaps, proving positivity from strict monotonicity. Distinct-gap runs are defined and shown to be downward-closed. The function h(x) is axiomatized with witness and optimality. Brun's divergence is stated both elementarily and as a Filter.Tendsto result. The Erdős conjectures use Real.log and Asymptotics.IsLittleO for rigorous formalization.
keyInsights: Prime gaps dₙ = pₙ₊₁ − pₙ encode the local distribution of primes
Brun's sieve ensures h(x) → ∞: long runs of distinct gaps exist
The lower bound conjecture (log x)^c is formalized with Real.log and real exponentiation
The upper bound h(x) = o(log x) is formalized using Asymptotics.IsLittleO
Pigeonhole principle gives h(x) ≤ x: at most x distinct positive values below x

sections.title: Prime Sequence and Gaps
sections.summary: Axiomatizes nthPrime with primality and strict monotonicity. Defines prime gaps and proves positivity, monotonicity, and nthPrime ≥ 2.

sections.title: Distinct Gap Runs
sections.summary: Defines IsDistinctRun and proves basic properties: empty/single runs are distinct, and distinct runs are downward-closed.

sections.title: Maximal Distinct Run Length h(x)
sections.summary: Axiomatizes h(x) with witness and optimality. Proves h(x) ≥ 1 for x ≥ 3 and monotonicity.

sections.title: Brun's Sieve Result
sections.summary: Brun's sieve divergence: h(x) → ∞. Proved in filter form as Tendsto atTop atTop.

sections.title: Erdős Conjectures (OPEN)
sections.summary: Lower bound (log x)^c with Real.log, upper bound o(log x) with IsLittleO, and derived consequences.

sections.title: Pigeonhole Upper Bound
sections.summary: h(x) ≤ x by pigeonhole: k distinct positive values bounded by M implies k ≤ M.

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem 852 investigates the growth rate of maximal distinct-gap runs among consecutive primes. While Brun's sieve shows h(x) → ∞, the conjectured growth rate between (log x)^c and o(log x) remains unresolved.
conclusion.implications: Determining h(x) would reveal deep structure in how prime gaps vary locally, connecting to the Hardy–Littlewood and Maier phenomena.
openQuestions: Is h(x) > (log x)^c for some constant c > 0?
What is the exact asymptotic growth rate of h(x)?
